newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat turns higher on harvest delays, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat turns higher on harvest delays, exports.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures shrugged off bearish input from soybeans and turned higher early, lifted by reports of harvest delays in Texas and Oklahoma and by weekly USDA export inspections data, traders said.

Cash grain dealers said a broad band of showers moved across the southern Plains over the weekend, bringing as much as six inches of rain to some parts of central Texas and causing further harvest delays.
A forecast map issued Monday morning by meteorolgists Weather Services Corp said rain was set to continue Monday and Tuesday in northeast Texas.

Wheat also drew strength from USDA's weekly export inspections data which came in above trade expectation. USDA said Monday 15,839,000 bushels of wheat were inspected for export in the week ended June 5, above trade expectation for seven million to 12 million bushels.
At 1006 CDT, wheat was up six to two cents, with July five cents higher at $3.64-1/2 per bushel.
